security.title: Missing Initialization of a Variable
security.description: The product does not initialize critical variables, which causes the execution environment to use unexpected values.

evidence.explanation: The static blobContainer field is declared without initialization and receives a value only when Index executes. Other action methods can be invoked before that action initializes it.

security.title: Use of Uninitialized Variable
security.description: The code uses a variable that has not been initialized, leading to unpredictable or unintended results.

evidence.explanation: The static blobContainer field initially has its default null value; UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll use it without ensuring Index has initialized it.

security.title: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
security.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

evidence.explanation: UploadAsync derives fileCount directly from the submitted Request.Files collection and loops over every entry without an application-level count limit. The configured request length limit is extremely high, so this input can control excessive repeated storage operations.

security.title: Improper Initialization
security.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.

evidence.explanation: The shared BlobContainerClient is initialized only as a side effect of Index. UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll assume it was initialized by a prior request, leaving the storage resource unavailable when those actions are invoked first.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: The static blobContainer field is assigned by each Index request and read by upload and delete requests without synchronization (lines 47, 63-66, 108, 135, and 158). Concurrent requests can observe and replace this shared reference without coordinated initialization.

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.Index creates the blob container with PublicAccessType.Blob. This grants anonymous read access to blobs in the container, exposing uploaded image content to anyone who can obtain a blob URI.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The upload and deletion operations can fail or alter stored content, but their exception handlers only place exception details in ViewData and return an error view. No audit or application logging records these events or outcomes.

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: In HomeController.UploadAsync (line 109), the client-supplied HttpPostedFile.FileName is passed to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path), which treats the value as a server-side filesystem path. The path is not constrained to an upload directory, so traversal elements may cause reads outside an intended upload location.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: In HomeController.UploadAsync (line 109), the client-provided file name is passed as a local path to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path). Relative traversal segments are not removed or checked against an allowed directory before the SDK reads the path.

security.title: Absolute Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: In HomeController.UploadAsync (line 109), the client-provided file name is passed to the BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) overload, which opens a local path. No check rejects an absolute path or confines it to a designated upload directory.

security.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
security.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

evidence.explanation: The DisplayFilesToUpload JavaScript function appends the user-controlled file.name value directly to an HTML string at line 80 and assigns the string to FilesToUpload.innerHTML at line 85. A crafted upload filename containing HTML can be interpreted as markup and script in the user's browser.
